claims.claim: Hartwell says Gene Wolfe is the writer with whom he had an editorial relationship for the majority of his career.
claims.source: David G. Hartwell, tribute in the Chicago Literary Hall of Fame Fuller Award program for Gene Wolfe, 2012
claims.quote: relationship for the majority of my career, longer than with any other
claims.page: Fuller Award program, tributes section (p. 18-19 of the program)

claims.claim: Hartwell says part of his reputation as an editor derives from the fact that he is Gene Wolfe's editor.
claims.source: David G. Hartwell, tribute in the Chicago Literary Hall of Fame Fuller Award program for Gene Wolfe, 2012
claims.quote: part of my reputation as an editor derives
claims.page: Fuller Award program, tributes section (p. 18-19 of the program)

claims.claim: Cooney says Wolfe's letter on her chapters named what she was doing well, dialogue and character, as well as the fault.
claims.source: C. S. E. Cooney, 'An Homage to my Honorary Grandfather', Ultan's Library, 2016
claims.quote: what I was doing well (Dialogue! Character!)

claims.claim: Cooney reports Wolfe agreeing to read her novel while refusing to promise any comment on it.
claims.source: C. S. E. Cooney, 'An Homage to my Honorary Grandfather', Ultan's Library, 2016
claims.quote: I can read it, but I can’t promise to say anything

claims.claim: Cooney says Wolfe told her that he too overwrites his early drafts.
claims.source: C. S. E. Cooney, 'An Homage to my Honorary Grandfather', Ultan's Library, 2016
claims.quote: Gene told me he does too
claims.page: memoir, on lumps of uncooked prose

claims.claim: Cooney reports Wolfe describing the last pass on a finished story as grooming it before sending it out again.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, quoted from memory by C. S. E. Cooney, Ultan's Library, 2016
claims.quote: Scrub her face. Give her a new dress.

claims.claim: Cooney reports Wolfe's rule that writers who do not subscribe to the magazines they submit to are cutting their own throats.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, quoted from memory by C. S. E. Cooney, Ultan's Library, 2016

claims.feature: other: what an editor made of him
claims.claim: Phillips reports that Knight also brought Wolfe to the Milford Writer's Workshop, where Wolfe had writing peers for the first time.
claims.source: Brian Phillips, 'Gene Wolfe Turned Science Fiction Into High Art', The Ringer, 25 April 2019
claims.quote: Knight also brings him to the Milford

claims.feature: other: an editor's letter as the turning point
claims.claim: Wolfe says Damon Knight was the only person who helped him with his writing when he really needed help.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Larry McCaffery, 'On Encompassing the Entire Universe', Science Fiction Studies #46 (vol. 15 part 3), November 1988
claims.quote: the only person who helped me with my writing when I really
claims.page: answer on the Fifth Head dedication

claims.feature: other: an editor's letter as the turning point
claims.claim: Wolfe says Knight's rejection letter for 'Trip Trap' told him where the story needed to change from one viewpoint to another and why.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Larry McCaffery, 'On Encompassing the Entire Universe', Science Fiction Studies #46 (vol. 15 part 3), November 1988
claims.quote: it needs to change here from viewpoint A to viewpoint
claims.page: answer on the Fifth Head dedication

claims.feature: other: an editor's letter as the turning point
claims.claim: Wolfe describes Knight's letter as carrying a long list of very sensible suggestions.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Larry McCaffery, 'On Encompassing the Entire Universe', Science Fiction Studies #46 (vol. 15 part 3), November 1988
claims.quote: list of very sensible suggestions of that sort
claims.page: answer on the Fifth Head dedication

claims.feature: other: an editor's letter as the turning point
claims.claim: Wolfe says that after reading Knight's letter he lay on the bed a long while and realised he was actually a writer now.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Larry McCaffery, 'On Encompassing the Entire Universe', Science Fiction Studies #46 (vol. 15 part 3), November 1988
claims.quote: on the bed for a long while, and I suddenly realized
claims.page: answer on the Fifth Head dedication

claims.feature: other: an editor's letter as the turning point
claims.claim: Wolfe says the bean line was Knight's own, written back to him: 'I didn't know I had grown you from a bean.'
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Larry McCaffery, 'On Encompassing the Entire Universe', Science Fiction Studies #46 (vol. 15 part 3), November 1988
claims.quote: I didn't know I had grown you from a bean
claims.page: answer on the Fifth Head dedication

claims.feature: other: the record that contradicts the fact
claims.claim: Wolfe says Frederik Pohl accepted the resubmitted 'The Mountains are Mice' with a letter praising a rewrite that had never happened.
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Larry McCaffery, 'On Encompassing the Entire Universe', Science Fiction Studies #46 (vol. 15 part 3), November 1988
claims.quote: My point is, of course, that there had been no re write
claims.page: answer on the Fifth Head dedication

claims.feature: other: the record that contradicts the fact
claims.claim: Wolfe quotes the acceptance letter as reading 'I'm glad you let me see this again. The re write has really improved it.'
claims.source: Gene Wolfe, interviewed by Larry McCaffery, 'On Encompassing the Entire Universe', Science Fiction Studies #46 (vol. 15 part 3), November 1988
claims.quote: I'm glad you let me see this again
claims.page: answer on the Fifth Head dedication
